notes: Fiscal year ended January 31, 2026 (Salesforce calls it fiscal 2026; data.js fy 'Jan 2026'). Documents read on sec.gov: FY2026 Form 10-K (accession 0001108524-26-000060, filed March 2, 2026) and 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001108524-26-000085, filed April 16, 2026). Dividends include dividend equivalents, as the cash-flow line says; XBRL also carries $1,605 million of dividends and equivalents declared, but the $1,587 million paid is used. Buybacks are the $12,596 million cash-flow line for fiscal 2026; the larger March 2026 accelerated share repurchase falls in fiscal 2027. Benioff's 22,791,882 shares include 880,310 shares from options and PRSUs vesting within 60 days and 10,000,000 shares held by the Marc Benioff Fund LLC; the proxy's 2.8% uses the 818,219,088 shares outstanding at March 25, 2026, after the accelerated repurchase. Holder asOf dates are the Schedule 13G filing dates the proxy cites; it gives no event dates. The Vanguard, BlackRock and State Street figures are from 2024 filings, so their percentages are stale share counts set against the smaller 2026 share base; the proxy also notes Vanguard now reports on a disaggregated basis. Salesforce completed its acquisition of Informatica in November 2025 (fiscal 2026 business combinations, net of cash acquired: $9,268 million). GEOGRAPHY: the 10-K says Americas revenue attributed to the United States was approximately 93% in each year.

ecosystem.notes: The 10-K has no flow measure, so measure is null. Both studies are IDC white papers sponsored by Salesforce and are model-based forecasts, not measured flows. The December 2023 paper estimates new revenue generated for Salesforce customers from AI-powered Salesforce clouds (it also gives $312 billion for 2022, rising to a forecast $948 billion in 2028); the $2.02 trillion is cumulative over 2022–2028. The September 2021 paper is the one that sizes the partner ecosystem itself (add-on apps, IT services, consulting, hardware and more sold around Salesforce), as a ratio to Salesforce's own revenue ($4.96 per $1 in 2021); it has no single money value, so value is null. IDC notes "the ecosystem may include companies that are not formal business partners of Salesforce". Neither study covers FY2026 actuals; no newer Salesforce-commissioned ecosystem study was used.

footprint.notes: Salesforce publishes no state, country or regional breakdown of employees, offices, investment or taxes for FY2026 (year ended Jan 31, 2026). The FY2026 10-K (Item 2) gives about 1.0 million sq ft of leased and owned property in the San Francisco Bay Area used for its executive and principal offices (plus about 2.2 million sq ft leased to others or available for lease), offices 'in various locations throughout the United States' and in Europe, North America, Asia, South America, Africa and Australia, and co-located data centers in the U.S., Europe and Asia, all without counts; it gives 83,334 employees in total with no geographic split. The FY26 Stakeholder Impact Report (checked Nov 24, 2026) has no geographic headcount either; its only location list is a water-risk map of priority sites, without values. The Hyderabad Centre of Excellence site is still cited from the FY25 Stakeholder Impact Report (still online), because the FY26 edition does not describe it. The IDC 'Salesforce Economy' white paper commissioned by Salesforce (Dec 2023) has no country table and only gives forecasts to 2028, so it was not used.

pay.notes: Employees: year-end count from the FY2026 10-K. Payroll: the 10-K gives no total of salaries, benefits or personnel costs (it describes employee-related costs only as components of cost of revenues and operating expenses), so the proxy's CEO pay ratio median is used.
